items.name: Dynamic Random Access Memory
items.definition: Standard volatile system memory. HBM is a specialized stacked form used on accelerators.

items.name: NAND flash
items.definition: Non-volatile storage memory used in SSDs and phones — separate from DRAM/HBM on GPUs.

items.name: High Bandwidth Memory
items.definition: Stacked DRAM placed next to the compute die for very high data bandwidth — a major cost on AI GPUs.

items.name: Solid State Drive
items.definition: Storage device built from NAND flash chips.

items.name: Double Data Rate memory
items.definition: Standard off-chip memory interface used in PCs and servers (e.g. DDR5).

items.name: High Bandwidth Memory 3 extended
items.definition: Latest HBM generation on NVIDIA H200 — faster and higher capacity than HBM3.

items.name: Surface Mount Technology
items.definition: Method of mounting components directly on PCB surfaces — used in module assembly.

items.name: Printed Circuit Board
items.definition: Board that connects and supports electronic components in a module or system.

items.name: Through-Silicon Via
items.definition: Vertical electrical connection through a silicon die — key to 3D stacking and HBM.

items.name: Outsourced Assembly, Test & Packaging
items.definition: Contractors that assemble, test, and pack finished chips (Foxconn, Amkor, etc.).

items.name: Wafer-Level Packaging
items.definition: Packaging chips while still on the wafer, before singulation into individual dies.

items.name: Chip on Wafer on Substrate
items.definition: TSMC advanced packaging: GPU die + HBM on a silicon interposer, mounted on a package substrate.

items.name: System in Package
items.definition: Multiple dies or components integrated into one package (often with HBM + logic).

items.name: Panel-Level Packaging
items.definition: Packaging many chips at panel scale rather than one die at a time — improves throughput.

items.name: Extreme Ultraviolet lithography
items.definition: 13.5 nm light for printing the finest chip features. ASML is the sole commercial supplier.

items.name: Deep Ultraviolet lithography
items.definition: Older-generation lithography (193 nm) still used for many chip layers.

items.name: NXE (EUV platform)
items.definition: ASML EUV scanner product line (e.g. NXE:3600) used at leading-edge fabs.

items.name: TWINSCAN
items.definition: ASML’s family of lithography scanner products (DUV and EUV systems).

items.name: NXT (DUV platform)
items.definition: ASML immersion DUV scanner product line for advanced nodes.

items.name: Optical Proximity Correction
items.definition: Software that pre-distorts mask patterns so printed shapes match design intent.

items.name: Argon Fluoride laser
items.definition: 193 nm DUV light source used in immersion lithography scanners.

items.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company
items.definition: World’s largest contract foundry; fabricates NVIDIA GPU dies and CoWoS packaging.

items.name: Systems on Silicon Manufacturing Company
items.definition: TSMC-affiliated wafer fab in Singapore.

items.name: Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing
items.definition: TSMC joint-venture fab in Kumamoto, Japan (with Sony and Denso).

items.name: Atomic Layer Deposition
items.definition: Ultra-thin, highly uniform film deposition — critical at advanced nodes.

items.name: Chemical Vapor Deposition
items.definition: Deposits thin films on wafers from gas-phase reactions.

items.name: Fabrication plant
items.definition: Clean-room factory where wafers are processed into chips.

items.name: Chemical Mechanical Polishing
items.definition: Process that planarizes wafer surfaces between fabrication steps.

items.name: Contract chip manufacturer
items.definition: Makes chips designed by others (fabless companies). TSMC is the dominant foundry here.

items.name: Radio Frequency
items.definition: Chip domains handling wireless and high-frequency analog signals.

items.name: Silicon on Insulator
items.definition: Wafer with thin silicon on an insulating layer — used in RF and low-power chips.

items.name: Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems
items.definition: Microscopic mechanical structures on silicon (sensors, actuators).

items.name: Gallium Nitride
items.definition: Wide-bandgap semiconductor for power electronics and some specialty wafers.

items.name: Silicon Carbide
items.definition: Wide-bandgap material for high-power and high-temperature devices.

items.name: Semiconductor intellectual property
items.definition: Licensed design blocks (CPU cores, interfaces) integrated into a chip.

items.name: Electronic Design Automation
items.definition: Software to design, simulate, and verify chips before manufacturing (Synopsys, Cadence).

items.name: Field Programmable Gate Array
items.definition: Reconfigurable chip that can be reprogrammed after manufacturing.

items.name: System on Chip
items.definition: Single chip integrating CPU, GPU, memory controllers, and other blocks.

items.name: Computational Fluid Dynamics
items.definition: Simulation of fluid/thermal behavior — used in chip and system cooling analysis.

items.name: Register Transfer Level
items.definition: Digital chip description level used before gate-level synthesis.

items.name: Design Rule Check
items.definition: Automated verification that layout meets fab manufacturing rules.

items.name: Application-Specific Integrated Circuit
items.definition: Custom chip designed for one application (vs. general-purpose CPU/GPU).

items.name: Layout vs. Schematic
items.definition: Verification that physical layout matches the intended circuit design.

items.name: Electromigration
items.definition: Metal wire degradation under current — a reliability concern in advanced chips.

items.name: Artificial Intelligence
items.definition: Machine learning workloads driving demand for GPUs, HBM, and advanced packaging.

items.name: Integrated Circuit
items.definition: Complete electronic circuit on a single chip.

items.name: Graphics Processing Unit
items.definition: Parallel processor for AI and graphics. H200 is NVIDIA’s data-center GPU in this report.

items.name: Graphics Processing Units
items.definition: Plural of GPU — parallel accelerators used for AI training and inference.

items.name: Integrated Circuits
items.definition: Plural of IC — chips fabricated on silicon wafers.

items.name: High Performance Computing
items.definition: Large-scale scientific and AI supercomputing — major GPU market segment.

items.name: Machine Learning
items.definition: Algorithms that learn from data — primary workload on NVIDIA data-center GPUs.

items.name: Central Processing Unit
items.definition: General-purpose processor core — often combined with accelerators in a system.

items.name: Bill of Materials
items.definition: Estimated dollar cost of components per finished product.

items.name: Virtual Reality
items.definition: Immersive display/compute market segment referenced in some filings.

items.name: Augmented Reality
items.definition: Overlay digital content on the real world — adjacent compute market.

items.name: ASML Holding
items.definition: Dutch company — monopoly supplier of EUV lithography systems.

items.name: KLA (inspection & metrology)
items.definition: Shorthand for KLA Corporation — wafer defect inspection and measurement tools.

items.name: Semiconductor Equipment and Materials International
items.definition: Industry association for chip supply chain; also used for equipment/materials sector.

items.name: KLA Corporation
items.definition: Leading process control and inspection equipment supplier (formerly KLA-Tencor).

items.name: Lam Research
items.definition: Major supplier of etch and deposition equipment for fabs.

items.name: Applied Materials
items.definition: Largest semiconductor equipment maker (deposition, etch, inspection).

items.name: Metrology and Inspection Business Unit
items.definition: KLA segment for process control and inspection products.

items.name: Component Inspection Business Unit
items.definition: KLA segment focused on component and reticle inspection.

items.name: SK Group / SK Hynix
items.definition: Korean conglomerate; SK Hynix is a primary HBM supplier in this chain.

items.name: Advanced Edge Business Unit
items.definition: Internal business segment referenced in equipment company filings.

items.name: Chip Data Business Unit
items.definition: Business unit referenced in semiconductor equipment filings.

items.name: Yangtze Memory Technologies Corp
items.definition: Chinese NAND flash manufacturer — cited in trade and supply-chain risk disclosures.

items.name: TSMC (ticker)
items.definition: NYSE ticker for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company.

items.name: Cadence Design Systems
items.definition: Major EDA and verification software vendor.

items.name: Micron Technology
items.definition: Memory manufacturer (DRAM and NAND).

items.name: NVIDIA (ticker)
items.definition: NASDAQ ticker symbol for NVIDIA Corporation.

items.name: Synopsys
items.definition: Major EDA and semiconductor IP vendor.

items.name: NVIDIA Corporation
items.definition: Designer of GPUs and AI accelerators (NVDA) — anchor company of this supply chain map.

items.name: Environmental, Social, and Governance
items.definition: Non-financial reporting on climate, workforce, and corporate governance.

items.name: Greenhouse Gas
items.definition: Emissions (CO₂ equivalent) tracked for climate reporting (Scope 1/2/3).

items.name: European Sustainability Reporting Standards
items.definition: EU mandatory sustainability disclosure framework.

items.name: Responsible Business Alliance
items.definition: Industry coalition setting labor and ethics standards for electronics supply chains.

items.name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
items.definition: Intergovernmental forum — OECD guidelines cited in responsible sourcing policies.

items.name: Environment, Health & Safety
items.definition: Workplace and environmental safety programs in fabs and factories.

items.name: Climate Change Mitigation
items.definition: EU taxonomy category for activities that reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

items.name: Science Based Targets initiative
items.definition: Framework for corporate emissions reduction targets aligned with climate science.

items.name: Semiconductor Climate Consortium
items.definition: Industry group working on semiconductor supply-chain emissions reduction.

items.name: Climate Change Adaptation
items.definition: EU taxonomy category for adapting to climate impacts.

items.name: International Labour Organization
items.definition: UN agency whose labor standards are referenced in supplier codes of conduct.

items.name: UN Global Compact
items.definition: UN corporate sustainability initiative referenced in ESG disclosures.

items.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
items.definition: Regulator publishing public company filings used as evidence in this report.

items.name: European Union
items.definition: Regional bloc whose regulations (CSRD, taxonomy) appear in sustainability filings.

items.name: Bureau of Industry and Security
items.definition: U.S. agency administering export controls on advanced semiconductors and tools.

items.name: CHIPS Act
items.definition: U.S. law providing incentives for domestic semiconductor manufacturing.

items.name: Passive Foreign Investment Company
items.definition: U.S. tax classification affecting foreign company shareholders.

items.name: European Economic Area
items.definition: EU plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway — referenced in geographic disclosures.

items.name: Export Administration Regulations
items.definition: U.S. Commerce Department rules governing dual-use technology exports.

items.name: International Traffic in Arms Regulations
items.definition: U.S. rules controlling export of defense-related technology.

items.name: American Depositary Shares
items.definition: Plural of ADS — how foreign stocks often trade on U.S. exchanges.

items.name: Accounting Standards Update
items.definition: FASB document proposing or amending GAAP rules.

items.name: Employee Stock Purchase Plan
items.definition: Program letting employees buy company stock at a discount.

items.name: Public Company Accounting Oversight Board
items.definition: U.S. body overseeing audits of public companies.

items.name: Long-Term Incentive
items.definition: Multi-year executive compensation tied to performance or stock.

items.name: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles
items.definition: U.S. accounting standards used in 10-K financial statements.

items.name: American Depositary Share
items.definition: U.S.-traded receipt representing shares of a foreign company.

items.name: eXtensible Business Reporting Language
items.definition: Machine-readable format for SEC financial filings.

items.name: Restricted Stock Units
items.definition: Plural of RSU — stock-based compensation awards.

items.name: Chief Operating Decision Maker
items.definition: Executive who allocates resources — defines reportable business segments.

items.name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act
items.definition: U.S. legislation referenced in recent tax and incentive disclosures.

items.name: Annual General Meeting
items.definition: Yearly shareholder meeting.

items.name: Internal Revenue Service
items.definition: U.S. tax authority referenced in tax footnotes.

items.name: International Financial Reporting Standards
items.definition: Global accounting standards used by many non-U.S. filers (e.g. ASML, TSMC).

items.name: Financial Accounting Standards Board
items.definition: U.S. body that sets GAAP accounting rules.

items.name: New York Stock Exchange
items.definition: U.S. stock exchange where some issuers in this dataset are listed.

items.name: Earnings Per Share
items.definition: Net income divided by shares outstanding — key profitability metric.

items.name: Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income
items.definition: Balance-sheet account for unrealized gains/losses outside net income.

items.name: Standalone Selling Price
items.definition: Revenue-recognition input for bundled hardware/software contracts.

items.name: Committee of Sponsoring Organizations
items.definition: Framework for internal control over financial reporting (COSO framework).

items.name: Fair Value Through Other Comprehensive Income
items.definition: IFRS accounting category for certain financial assets.

items.name: Short-Term Incentive
items.definition: Annual bonus or performance pay for executives and employees.

items.name: Double Materiality Assessment
items.definition: ESG process assessing impact on business and on society/environment.

items.name: Secured Overnight Financing Rate
items.definition: U.S. benchmark interest rate used in loan agreements.

items.name: International Organization for Standardization
items.definition: Body issuing standards (e.g. ISO 14001 environmental management).

items.name: Enterprise Risk Management

items.name: Enterprise Resource Planning

items.name: Total Shareholder Return
